pr.title: Use a neutral example for a drawer's grouped threads
pr.head: 098ea8f362bc1fc59b53c3b72a39fa34f81a90f6

summary: Projector's panel lists the session's pull requests above the prompt. Opening a pull request's drawer shows its unresolved review threads, gathered under the file each thread is on. Each file is a line you can open to see its threads, one line per thread: the line number, who opened it, outdated when a later push moved the code, and the start of its first comment.

Both the user documentation for that drawer and the test that checks how threads are grouped used a real file path and real finding titles from another repository. Projector is a public framework that keeps its examples free of other people's projects, so this change replaces them with a made-up file, src/audio/player.ts, and made-up findings. Nothing else changes: the panel's code is untouched, and both examples keep their shape.

groups.title: The drawer example in the docs and the test
groups.kicker: Swap the sample path, line numbers, and finding titles
intro: The docs example shows one open file with two threads, the second outdated, above a collapsed file. The test feeds the drawer five threads across three files and checks the order the drawer draws them in: files in the order of each file's oldest thread, and threads oldest first within a file, not sorted by line number.

To prove the second rule, the test needs one file whose threads' line numbers sort differently from the order they arrived in. The old numbers, 1875, 1902, 1897, did that, and the new ones, 120, 188, 154, keep the same pattern.

files.note: The sample drawer under the section on a pull request's drawer, with the new path and finding titles.

checks.text: The reviewer rendered this example's input through the drawer in a temporary test: two threads on src/audio/player.ts, the second outdated, and one on docs/notes.md. With the first file opened, the drawer drew these four lines exactly.

files.note: The grouping test's input threads and the lines it expects, with the new path, line numbers, and titles.

checks.text: The test still catches a broken grouping. In the review, sorting each file's threads by line number made this test fail, and sorting files by path made it and two other drawer tests fail.
The new data names no person, account, repository, or organization. grace and bob are placeholder logins used throughout this test file.
